sources.excerpt: STOMP BOX STEALS: OVERDRIVE- CIRCLE OF TONE Quad Damage ...another mystery pedal? STOMP BOX STEALS Since 2015 NEW PEDALS EVERY DAY! Over 4500 REVIEWS! I use other reviewers vids & then critique from them __ If a pedal appears killer I buy one __ I try it out & update the Post__ If the pedal is SH@T I literally say so!__ I publish the street price a no brainer but few do. __ I save you time finding the best pedals & you get a second opinion. __OVER 4 MILLION VISTORS__ NO ONE OWNS ME___ I MAKE ZERO $ FROM THIS Paul L. Ewing / LENARD Re-Inventions View my complete profile Thursday, July 10, 2025 OVERDRIVE- CIRCLE OF TONE Quad Damage ...another mystery pedal? QUAD DAMAGE   CIRCLE Of TONE   $50.00 USD I stumble on to this pedal. Another mystery pedal found on a   Brit   site, made in Canada but the only video is  Brazilian so   it is in   Portuguese. I can not find the company or any   other pedals???😕 Well it appears to be a medium to high gain OD with an Amp   in a box vibe.  The layout is Volume, Gain and Tone with a Mid to  either sweep   or boost, or both, lol.             C ONCLUSION__ it sounds damn good. It has a rich warm sound and   is tight   and punchy with great string definition. It does a very nice wall of sound. It looks like   a better made upmarket pedal. Worth a shot?     Posted by Paul L. Ewing / LENARD Re-Inventions at 1:49 AM Email This BlogThis! Share to X Share to Facebook Share to Pinterest No comments: Post a Comment Newer Post Older Post Home View mobile version Subscribe to: Post Comments (Atom) About Me Paul L. Ewing / LENARD Re-Inventions I have spent years in the music biz as a guitarist. I played in London England with the Prog rock band Tallis. I have always been curious in what makes an electric guitar, amp or pedal great. I was fortunate enough to make contacts with builders worldwide. I even had friends... old timers from the Gibson Kalamazoo factory. I learnt my craft from those that invented the electric guitars that we still love today. My design sensibility says "If it is not broke don't fix it!!!" I also feel the guitar is a tool! It is not a wall hanger display. Keep it simple! Keep to what works! As for pedals. I have many friends that are popular YouTubers as well as Independent pedal builders that give me a heads up about new things even before the release date. This way you can find it here first.
